## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** The change does what the description says, and no defect was found in the tested scope. The catalog-wide numbers reproduce against xkeyboard-config 2.48: 752 distinct descriptions, exactly 26 changed labels, and no label that becomes shared with a different layout. The same 26 labels change against 2.47 (749 descriptions). Every changed label comes from an explicit `Latin` or `Cyrillic` qualifier, and the compound terms named in the description (`Latin American`, `Latin-9 only`, Kurdish `Latin Q` and `Arabic-Latin`) keep their current labels. The updated `test/shell.d/keyboard-layout-test.sh` passes with 74 assertions on the PR head, and 15 of the new script assertions fail against the base model, so the tests guard the new rule.

| Layout (xkeyboard-config 2.48) | Base | PR |
|---|---|---|
| `rs`: Serbian | SR | SR |
| `rs(latin)`: Serbian (Latin) | SR | SRL |
| `me(cyrillic)`: Montenegrin (Cyrillic) | SR | SRC |
| `by(latin)`: Belarusian (Latin) | BY | BYL |
| `lv(modern)` / `lv(modern-cyr)`: Latvian (Modern Latin / Modern Cyrillic) | LV / LV | LVL / LVC |
| `latam`: Spanish (Latin American) | ES | ES |

### Script suffix follows description wording, not the layout's script

The suffix is added only when the description text names `Latin` or `Cyrillic`. Base layouts whose script is implied rather than named keep the two-letter label, even where a sibling of the same script gains a suffix:

```text
layout           script in symbols file      label
rs               Cyrillic                    SR
rs(yz)           Cyrillic                    SRC
me               Latin (includes rs(latin))  SR
me(latinyz)      Latin                       SRL
ph               Latin                       PH
ph(qwerty-bay)   Baybayin                    PH
ph(dvorak)       Latin                       PHL
```

**Impact:** The main case in the description, `rs` against `rs(latin)`, now reads SR against SRL as intended. Two smaller inconsistencies remain. First, unchanged from base: `rs` (Cyrillic) and `me` (Latin) both still read SR, and `ph` (Latin) and the Baybayin `ph` variants all read PH. Second, new with this change: some same-script pairs that used to share a label now differ: `me` reads SR while its Latin variants read SRL, and `ph` reads PH while its Latin-qualified variants read PHL. The tooltip still shows the full layout name.

**Suggested change:** If the metadata-only approach is the intended trade-off, the new code comment could say so. The comment currently reads "When a two-letter brief covers multiple scripts", but the code adds the letter for any two-letter brief whose description names Latin or Cyrillic. That is why Indonesian (IDL), Chuvash (RUL) and the Filipino Latin variants (PHL) also change. For example: "When the description explicitly names Latin or Cyrillic, a two-letter brief gains that script's initial; layouts whose script is only implied keep the bare brief." An optional, untested approach, if that consistency is wanted: a small default-script entry for `me` so that it reads SRL.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the pinned head `df75fa3`. The repository keyboard-layout test was run in an isolated sandbox with Node against the head model and the base model. Catalog results come from xkeyboard-config 2.47 and 2.48 release data, parsed by an emulation of libxkbcommon's `xkbcli list --load-exotic` (brief inheritance, de-duplication, base then exotic order), not by the real binary. Layout scripts were read from the xkeyboard-config `symbols` files. Not tested on a running desktop or under the QML JavaScript engine.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
